hamin_ending_someday.024: You stop at the railing. He puts himself on the side the wind's coming from. You notice. You let him, this once, and make a note to take the next one.
hamin_ending_someday.025: I should say it properly. Out loud. I've been saying it with cans all night.
hamin_ending_someday.026: It's not a big deal, but— {p}no. It's a big deal.
hamin_ending_someday.027: I like you. {p}Not as weather. Not as a cup. I like you. I checked it twice, and it held both times.
hamin_ending_someday.028: I like you too. I checked it once. I didn't need the second time.
hamin_ending_someday.029: He laughs, the open one, head down, and the river takes it and doesn't give it back.
hamin_ending_someday.030: Then can I say the other thing? It's going to sound like the opposite. It isn't.
hamin_ending_someday.032: I've had one night of someone asking what I want. I'm not good at it yet. I said "egg sandwich" like it was a confession.
hamin_ending_someday.033: I don't want to hand you someone who's still working out how to have a preference.
hamin_ending_someday.034: I want to get better at it. And I want you to be there while I do. Not waiting. Just there.
hamin_ending_someday.035: "I've never stayed anywhere long enough for something to arrive slowly. I want to find out what that's like."
hamin_ending_someday.037: I've done fast. Fast is forty minutes and a box. I want the other one.
hamin_ending_someday.038: …Then we want the same thing. I've never been able to say that sentence before.
hamin_ending_someday.039: "Good. I've only just unpacked the kettle. One thing at a time."
hamin_ending_someday.042: I respect that. {p}I'll be second. I'm a very good second. I'll work my way up.
hamin_ending_someday.043: Move round to the windward side of him, so the wind reaches you first instead.
hamin_ending_someday.044: He starts to protest. Then he understands what you're saying, and stops.
hamin_ending_someday.046: For as long as it takes. That's the point.
hamin_ending_someday.047: He takes something out of his pocket. The roll of masking tape from the lost property box. The marker. Of course he kept them.
hamin_ending_someday.048: I want it labelled. So it isn't just a feeling in a box.
hamin_ending_someday.049: He tears off a strip, presses it to the railing, and writes. Small square capitals. He isn't hiding this one with his arm.
hamin_ending_someday.050: JULY. BUSAN. THE BEACH BY THE SEAWALL. 23:41.
hamin_ending_someday.051: That's when the recording starts. I'd like to start the next one at the same minute.
hamin_ending_someday.052: Ten months. It's a long time. It isn't a test. I'll see you tomorrow, and on Tuesday, and I'll still know your order.
hamin_ending_someday.053: But on that beach, at that minute, I'd like to say "stay a bit" first. Before the can. As someone who's had some practice.
hamin_ending_someday.055: He writes a second line under the first.
hamin_ending_someday.056: BRING: ONE PEACH ICED TEA. ONE CORN TEA. A COAT, BECAUSE YOU WON'T.
hamin_ending_someday.057: BRING: ONE HOT CHOCOLATE, IF IT'S NOT SOLD OUT. ONE CORN TEA. A COAT, BECAUSE YOU WON'T.
hamin_ending_someday.058: BRING: ONE BLACK COFFEE. ONE CORN TEA. A COAT, BECAUSE YOU WON'T.
hamin_ending_someday.059: BRING: ONE GRAPE SODA. ONE CORN TEA. A COAT, BECAUSE YOU WON'T.
hamin_ending_someday.060: I'll buy them. You just have to be shivering thirty metres down the beach. For accuracy.
hamin_ending_someday.061: And you'll walk past me to the machine.
hamin_ending_someday.062: And then I'll come back. {p}That's the part I'm changing.
hamin_ending_someday.063: He peels the label off the railing, carefully, so it doesn't tear, and sticks it to the back of your phone. He presses the edges flat with his thumb.
hamin_ending_someday.064: NOT LOST. I ran out of room to write it. It's implied.
hamin_ending_someday.065: You have always left in spring. July is on the far side of spring. You will have to stay through the whole of it to get there, and you find that you've already decided to.
hamin_ending_someday.066: It's louder in the morning. The river.
hamin_ending_someday.068: Everything else is just waking up.
hamin_ending_someday.069: His shoulder is next to yours on the railing. Not touching. Close enough that it's a promise and not a question.
hamin_ending_someday.070: Below you, the river goes on towards the sea, the long way round, in no hurry at all. It gets there every time.
